what: Nokia makes telecom network equipment: mobile base stations, optical and IP routing gear for fixed networks, and it licenses its patents to phone makers. It no longer makes phones itself.
customers: Mobile operators worldwide, fixed broadband providers, large enterprises, and handset makers paying patent licences.
money: optical, IP routing and fixed broadband equipment
radio access equipment for mobile operators
moat: Patents essential to mobile standards, which earn royalties regardless of whose equipment is sold, plus one of only three Western suppliers operators can choose.
risks: Mobile operator capital spending has been weak for two years
Operating margin of about 4% is thin
It competes against Huawei on price in markets that allow it
Revenue fell about 3% a year over three years before last year's recovery
opportunities: Optical and IP equipment is being bought by data centre operators, a new customer type
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
watch: Network Infrastructure orders from data centre customers and patent licensing renewals.
